FILINGS: the day's read had to be repeated twice before it was complete (2,282 of 2,287 rows against 531 and 699 on the first two attempts), and the completeness mattered - all four researched names came from rows the truncated reads had dropped. Of the day's four hard triggers, three were declined on their own documents: ORIRAIL's order is Rs 1.65 cr, under 1% of a year's sales and its seventh order filing in 80 days; ELITECON's is a framework agreement with an indicative ceiling, on a stock down 96% in a year with two BSE SOP-fine notices; TGVSL's is a 5 MWp captive solar addition with no rupee value. The one published, TRISHAKT, is published at low confidence and with its direction corrected: BSE filed it as an order received, but the release says Trishakti ISSUED a Rs 105.39 cr purchase order to XCMG for 60 machines. It is the largest number of the day relative to the business - 3.8x a trailing year's revenue - on a company compounding revenue at 252% YoY with near-100% utilisation, and the model built from its own revenue per machine-year says the fleet nearly doubling still leaves a forward PE near 35x because depreciation triples. The balance sheet is where it would break: Rs 156.01 cr of other current financial liabilities against Rs 0.58 cr of cash, a current ratio of 0.37x, and a resolution to lift the borrowing limit to Rs 1,000 cr. Nine names closed at 65-day highs on 3.2x to 35.3x their median volume with no filing at all; all nine were watch-listed, not researched, per runbook 144b.
